integrity: The complete 1974 Field–Noyes article was inspected across all pages containing the five-step Oregonator, dimensional equations, dimensionless reduction, numerical limit cycle, stiff approximation, and normal-mode analysis. The exact equations and historical numerical constants used in the specialization were taken from that full source. Later Oregonator bifurcation and wave literature was compared at statement level, and a modern global-Hopf source supplied the primary differential-dynamics classification. The conditional identities and equality cases were independently reconstructed from stationarity and replayed with the packaged exact checker.
scientific_limitations: The theorem concerns compactly supported invariant probability measures and does not prove existence or uniqueness of a limit cycle for arbitrary parameters.
The rational X-nullcline formula should be interpreted through its undivided identity at the slice k1*A=k2*X.
The result constrains conditional means and second moments but not the full invariant density, period, or Floquet multipliers.
The complete modern global-Hopf article was unavailable in the inspected source; its abstract, classification, and statement were compared.
A differently phrased short generator identity could remain in unindexed chemical-kinetics literature.
title: Exact stationary nullcline calibration and coupled speed defects in the Oregonator
